questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Reason about parallel lines and transversals
questions.stem: If alternate interior angles are unequal, what follows?

options.text: The lines are parallel anyway
options.misconception: ignores the converse of alternate interior angles

options.text: The lines are not parallel
The transversal must be perpendicular
The angles must be complementary

questions.explanation: Equal alternate interior angles imply parallel lines; unequal ones imply non-parallel. Perpendicularity would require 90°. Complementarity is unrelated.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute a third angle in a triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has angles 25° and 95°; what is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Triangle angles sum to 180°. 180° − 25° − 95° = 60°. A value of 120° would subtract only 60°.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute a complement in a bracket
questions.stem: A bracket angle measures 12°; what is its complement?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°. 90° − 12° = 78°. A value of 168° would use 180° instead of 90°.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute a corresponding angle
questions.stem: Parallel beams are cut by a transversal at 51°; what is the corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal for parallel lines. The angle is 51°. A value of 129° would be the supplementary adjacent angle.
